question: Should spawned-session lineage standardize on the existing parent edge with derived root/depth, or add persisted `rootSessionKey` and a new durable session-chain `traceId`?
rationale: Either choice becomes persisted session state and a public Gateway/tool contract; source inspection cannot determine the intended identity lifetime or whether diagnostic/task identifiers should be reused.

options.title: Canonical parent, derived lineage
options.body: Normalize spawnedBy and parentSessionKey into one authoritative parent relationship, derive root/depth for reads, and avoid a new trace identifier unless a separate lifetime is proven.

options.title: Persist all four fields
options.body: Add parent, root, depth, and chain trace fields with explicit creation, reset, adoption, access-control, and migration semantics.

options.title: Defer new contract
options.body: Keep current parent/depth metadata and postpone broader chain APIs and visualization until a durable identity model is selected.

recommendation.title: Canonical parent, derived lineage
recommendation.body: Normalize spawnedBy and parentSessionKey into one authoritative parent relationship, derive root/depth for reads, and avoid a new trace identifier unless a separate lifetime is proven.
